_comment: Every LLVM 23 function/parameter attribute the corpus does not name gets an answer here: a chapter that teaches it, or a reason it is out of scope. `emitted_by` records the recipe that was actually run against clang 23.1.1 to produce the attribute -- 'not reproduced' means the listed recipes emitted nothing, which is itself the reason. Checked by tools/verify-langref-delta.py.

coro_only_destroy_when_complete.reason: Not reproduced: clang 23.1.1 emitted nothing for the recipes tried, so the corpus has no verified way to show a reader where it comes from. Teaching it would mean describing IR this toolchain does not produce.

disable_sanitizer_instrumentation.reason: An opt-out marker for sanitizer instrumentation, and not reproducible here: clang 23 emitted none even under -fsanitize=address. Out of scope on the same boundary as the rest of the sanitizer family -- the corpus teaches sanitizers by the shape of the instrumentation they insert, not by the attributes that request or suppress it.

inlinehint.reason: Not reproduced: clang 23.1.1 emitted nothing for the recipes tried, so the corpus has no verified way to show a reader where it comes from. Teaching it would mean describing IR this toolchain does not produce.

naked.reason: Suppresses prologue and epilogue entirely, which makes the function's body inline assembly by necessity. 13-advanced-ir teaches inline asm as the mechanism; a function with no ABI is a niche of that niche.

noredzone.reason: A target ABI switch. The red zone itself is taught in 19-hardware-aware as a calling-convention fact; the attribute only relays the flag.

nosanitize_coverage.reason: An opt-in sanitizer marker: it tells a later pass to instrument the function, and carries no meaning for anyone reading ordinary IR. The corpus teaches sanitizers by the shape of the instrumentation they insert, not by the attribute that requests it -- the same boundary the 18->23 delta table draws for sanitize_type and sanitize_realtime.

speculative_load_hardening.reason: A Spectre mitigation that rewrites branches into data dependencies. The transformation is worth teaching and the attribute that requests it is not; it belongs with the mitigation, not with the language.

ssp.reason: The weakest member of the stack-protector family, out of scope for the same reason as sspstrong and sspreq: it selects which functions get a guard, and says nothing about the IR a reader is learning to read.

sspreq.reason: A stack-protection request, emitted verbatim from the build flag. It changes the prologue a backend writes, not the meaning of the IR; 19-hardware-aware teaches the prologue.

sspstrong.reason: The heuristic sibling of sspreq, and out of scope for the same reason: it selects which functions get a guard, and says nothing about the IR.
